verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced what the reviewer saw: the tile does say 'Rex: a faint flicker' next to 'about the same as a Toyota Corolla at 100 km/h' for the all-out Collide hit (499 kJ). It reads the same at dials of 10^5, 10^9 and 10^14 kg, and the same with Rex charging. But the two statements do not contradict each other. Both are true, and the page follows the canon and the approved brief.

(1) The canon ruling of 14 Oct 2026 says 'a faint flicker below a car crash', and the anchor is the rung energy_corolla_100kmh_kinetic at 517.1 kJ. 499 kJ is 3.5% below that rung. So under canon it gets a faint flicker, exactly as the card says: 'Below a car crash he shows a faint flicker (canon)'.

(2) 'About the same as' is compare()'s 15% band. It describes the energy, not the glow level. An energy can be just below a threshold and also about the same as it.

(3) The brief's own table gives 'faint flicker: 7.3 kJ to 517 kJ'. Its worked example gives 0.47 MJ as 'a faint flicker, just under a flicker', and 470 kJ sits inside the same 'about the same' band (470/517 = 0.91 > 1/1.15 = 0.87). So the approved plan already labelled this kind of energy a faint flicker.

(4) Decision 14 in the README states it outright: 'everything from the floor up to a car crash is "a faint flicker" (canon)'.

(5) The glow on the art does not jump at the line. Its strength is 0.0924 at 499.5 kJ against 0.0932 at the flicker. Only the word changes, as with any named category.

The proposed fix would not remove the tension. It would just move it: 451–517 kJ would become 'about a flicker' while still below the car crash. That breaks the card's 'Below a car crash he shows a faint flicker (canon)', the brief's table and the canon ruling as written. This is a recorded decision justified by canon, not a defect.

Optional, not required: if the owner wants the closeness spelled out, the faint-flicker word could add 'just under a flicker' when compare() calls the energy the same as the flicker rung.

verdict.reasoning:
Reproduced on Throw (a car), Stomp, Clap (Silent strike) and the Wrestle throw, all at unlimited strength and all-out. The new Shimmer tile reads '...: unlimited strength has no physical answer here, so there is no figure.' Each of those tabs does give the answer:
- Throw: 'Launch: light speed (to the last digit)', 'Energy in the car ∞ J, unbounded energy', 'The energy is unbounded.'
- Stomp: 'Energy taken back ∞ J, it would have broken the ground: unbounded energy', 'The unbounded energy that would have blasted a crater is taken back to the endless ocean.'
- Clap: 'Silent strike: the clap's energy: ∞ J (unbounded energy) absorbed.'

On this page and in the engine, 'no physical answer' is a term of art. It means the canon's paradox, or a case the lab can't model, where nothing is worked out. Examples: app.html:5237 'has no physical answer here (the canon's ruling), so the lab can't judge its harm' (nearly the same words), :3109 'no physical answer and the lab can't model it', and the Collide paradox verdicts. The build's own engine-report.md says: 'A figure with no physical answer (the paradox, an undefined result) adds nothing.'

The engine bears that out. The paradox Collide (Rex bolted) gives takenBack E = 0, so no tile appears. The unlimited throw gives E = Infinity with unbounded: true. So the tile uses the paradox's label for exactly the case the engine treats as not a paradox. A reader is told the run has no answer while the same tab gives one. That is an unsupported claim and a contradiction between the page text and the engine's result.

The recorded decision (README: 'At unlimited strength it says the energy is unbounded, in words: there is no figure') covers saying 'unbounded' and showing no figure. It does not cover the 'no physical answer' clause. The phrase is new in this pull request (it does not appear in claude/canon-4-contests), and test/shots.js pr5 [unbounded] asserts the wrong wording. Severity is minor: it is a copy error with no wrong number.

findings.title: The shimmer card gives the wrong reason for "roughly", and states the disputed scale's steps more precisely than the data supports
findings.location: rex-strength-lab/src/static-data.js:22 ("That energy is disputed, so the flare and the steps near it are rough"); src/app.html:5701 (SHIM steps text)
findings.evidence: Rendered card: "…a blinding flare at the asteroid that killed the dinosaurs (about 5 × 10²³ J). That energy is disputed, so the flare and the steps near it are rough (“roughly”). … “faint glow” at about 1.6 × 10¹⁰ J …, “glow” at about 5.1 × 10¹⁴ J …, “bright” at roughly 2 × 10¹⁹ J (roughly 30% of the heat an average hurricane releases in a day)". In the code (ladder.js glow(), README decision 13), a step says "roughly" only when the rung compare() words it against is rough. The ¾ step is "roughly" because of the hurricane rung, not the flare. The ¼ and ½ steps hang on the flare's energy just as much (each is 10^(L0 + level × span)), yet they say "about", to two figures. The fact (research/final-energy.json, energy_chicxulub_impact, status "disputed", high_si 1.674e25 J, about 33×) puts the ½ step at 2.9 × 10¹⁵ J (5.8× higher), the ¼ step at 3.9 × 10¹⁰ J (2.4×) and the ¾ step at 2.2 × 10²⁰ J (14×). README Known limits admits this ("the quarter and half steps' energies hang on the flare too, so they are less firm than 'about' suggests"), but the page tells readers the opposite.
findings.expected: Honest labelling: the card should give the actual rule, or say that every step's energy rests on the disputed flare. Step energies should be rounded to what the data supports (CLAUDE.md: "Round to what the data supports").
findings.fix: Card: "That energy is disputed (one older estimate is about 33 times higher), and every step's energy is set by it, so all of them are rough; the tile says 'roughly' where the ladder's own rule does (the flare, and the ¾ step beside the rough hurricane rung)." Give the steps to one figure: "roughly 2 × 10¹⁰ J", "roughly 5 × 10¹⁴ J", "roughly 2 × 10¹⁹ J".

verdict.reasoning: The text is as quoted, but I don't count it as a defect. (1) The card's description of what is rough matches what the code marks. ladder.js glow() marks exactly two items 'roughly': the flare, and the ¾ step at 1.59e19 J, whose comparison rung is the rough hurricane rung. The ¾ step is also the step nearest the flare, so 'the flare and the steps near it are rough' holds for every step on the current data. No input makes the card's reason and the code's rule disagree. The card's wording also follows the brief's own letter ('so the page says "about" for the flare and the steps near it'). (2) The step energies are definitions, not measurements. They are log points between the Corolla rung and canon's own anchor: the 14 Oct ruling gives the flare as 'a dinosaur-killer-scale hit (about 5 × 10²³ J)'. Giving a definition to two figures is not false precision. (3) The 33× spread rests on the 1.674e25 J high, which the fact's own note dates to Sharpton & Marin 1997, 'from a ~300 km crater … sizes since revised down'. The modern sources in the same fact give 4.0–6.7e23 J (Morgan et al. 2022) and 4.9–9.2e23 J (Collins et al. 2020), within 2×, the ladder's own threshold for 'rough'. On that spread the ¼ and ½ steps would move by under about 1.2× and 1.4×, so 'about' is supportable. (4) The conservative reading, that the ¼ and ½ steps hang on the flare too, is recorded in README Known limits, where the owner will see it.

findings.location: rex-strength-lab/src/engine.js, realAirThrow: `Math.max(0, r.Eobj + tbPE(...) - keFromV(f0.vImpact, obj.m))` with f0 launched at r.vOut. The never-lands branch has the same problem (it returns r.Eobj), and so does r.dragLoss0, which uses the same formula.
findings.evidence:

The full-drag flight from vOut loses 24.7 kJ to the air. Eobj − KE(vOut) = 102 kJ, which is G·M·m/r0, the depth of his well.

findings.expected: Real air's take is KE(vOut) + PE(release) − KE(vImpact) = 24.7 kJ. The climb against his own pull is gravitational energy, not drag, and nothing takes it back.
findings.fix: In realAirThrow, use keFromV(r.vOut, obj.m) in place of r.Eobj, in both the landed branch and the never-lands branch. Don't reuse r.dragLoss0 when self-gravity is on. Add a 9c case with a dense Rex, for example 10^12 kg at 10 ft, dial 10^12 kg: expect about 24.7 kJ.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced.
